title: Analysis of acute mastoiditis, sinugenic orbital complications, and oto- and sinugenic central complications before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
summary:
Middle ear infections and sinusitis can have far-reaching complications. For example, a middle ear infection can lead to meningitis. Current scientific studies report that, likely due to the quarantine and hygiene measures implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic, there has been an increase in the incidence of these serious complications since the pandemic ended. There is also evidence that the pathogens causing these complications have changed. These changes may, for example, lead to pathogens becoming resistant to certain antibiotics. It is also possible that previously less relevant pathogens have gained clinical significance, or that formerly relevant pathogens are occurring less frequently.

The main objective of this study is to identify the pathogens responsible for acute mastoiditis and central and orbital complications and to investigate their resistance patterns. Furthermore, the study aims to identify risk constellations with the goal of improving care in emergency departments by enabling early detection of the risk of severe infections and better protecting patients from them.

The study includes all patients who underwent surgery at the University Hospital Bonn's Department of Otolaryngology due to the aforementioned complications. The observation period extends from July 1, 2010, to October 1, 2025. This observation period allows for a comparison of cases before the COVID-19 pandemic with cases during and after the pandemic. The case analysis is conducted exclusively retrospectively.

interventions.name: All patients who underwent surgery performed by the Department of Otorhinolaryngology  for mastoiditis, oto- or sinugenic intracranial complications, or sinugenic orbital complications at the University Hospital Bonn between July 1, 2010, and October 1, 2025, will be included. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The only inclusion criterion is surgical treatment by the Department of Otolaryngology at the University Hospital Bonn in cases of acute mastoiditis, oto- or sinugenic central complication, or sinugenic orbital complication.
Exclusion criteria:
Indication of incorrect coding or recording of an incorrect treatment diagnosis in the computer information system.
